title: Access & Credential Sprint Runbook (RBAC v2 + SIEM Export)
content:
Purpose and intent:
This working runbook consolidates sprint-level tasks and operational run steps for Secrets Management across RBAC v2 rollout, audit log schema standardization, SIEM export mapping, and evidence-automation for credential rotations and break-glass events. This is a pragmatic engineering-first doc — expect TO-DOs and integration notes.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Vaulting patterns and operational steps for short/medium/long-lived credentials
- Rotation cadence recommendations and automation hooks (CI/CD + webhook consumers)
- Break-glass workflow: emergency access + postmortem evidence collection
- RBAC v2 considerations: roles, role inheritance, temporary elevation
- Audit / log schema for secrets operations (create/read/update/delete/rotate/evict)
- SIEM export field mapping and example events
- Credential inventory hygiene and decommission playbook

Quick summary for on-call: (copy into Slack snippet)
1) If a credential is compromised or suspected: immediately revoke the secret in Vault (vault kv metadata destroy / rotate path), escalate to SecOps pager, create a 'cred-incident-<yyyyMMdd>' ticket and tag owner.
2) Trigger automated evidence collection job (see 'evidence-collector' pipeline) and attach generated artifact to the ticket.
3) If access was via break-glass token, mark 'break_glass:true' in incident metadata and capture the ephemeral session recording link.

Operational run steps (detailed)
A. Revocation & Short-term rotation (0-4 hours)
- Identify key material scope: app credential / service token / machine user key.
- Use vault CLI to revoke and replace: vault kv put secret/<path> value=<new> metadata=rotation="manual-YYYYMMDD"
- Run dependent-reload: curl -X POST https://infra-api/internal/reload-config?service=SERVICE_NAME or trigger the service's rollout pipeline.
- Kick off the evidence-collector job (k8s job: sec-evidence-collector --ticket cred-incident-123) to snapshot current ACLs, active sessions, and recent audit events.
- Update ticket with owner, new secret location, and list of downstream consumers (from inventory).

B. Scheduled rotation (24 hours to weeks)
- Default rotation windows: production database passwords = 30 days, service tokens = 14 days, ephemeral deploy keys = 7 days, long-lived HSM keys = 365 days (rotate policy + key versioning).
- Rotation automation pattern: cron-triggered rotation-controller -> create new version in Vault -> run smoke tests in canary -> swap secret references via feature-flagged rollout -> deprecate old version (ttl) -> archive audit evidence.
- Always generate a rotation report: rotation_controller produces JSON with fields (rotation_id, target_path, old_version, new_version, start_ts, end_ts, outcome, smoke_test_url) and posts to Confluence and SIEM.

Break-glass workflow (emergency access)
- Pre-reqs: break-glass role exists in RBAC v2 with 2FA and approval flow (approver list maintained by SecOps).
- Trigger: engineer requests break-glass via SecOps console -> automated 2-of-3 approver ping -> if approved, issue temporary token with TTL <= 1 hour and 'break_glass:true' metadata.
- During session: sessions are recorded, all Vault audit events for that token are flagged (break_glass=true) and exported immediately to SIEM.
- After session: mandatory postmortem within 72 hours; attach session recording, list of secrets accessed, and justification to ticket.

RBAC v2 notes and constraints
- Roles should be coarse-grained for orgs: vault-reader, vault-writer, vault-rotate, vault-breakglass-approver, vault-admin. Avoid per-service roles unless justified by compliance.
- Implement role inheritance for product teams: team-role -> product-role -> env-role (prod/staging). Prefer dynamic role binding for ephemeral workers (OIDC).
- Audit-related requirement: every role change must create a labeled audit event: {event_type: "role_assignment", actor, target_role, binding_ttl, request_id}. These events are essential for evidence automation.
- Temporary elevation pattern: request -> approval chain -> issue short-lived role-binding with expiration and recorded justification.

Audit log schema (secrets-focused) - required fields
- timestamp: ISO-8601
- event_id: UUID
- event_type: one of {secret_create, secret_read, secret_update, secret_delete, secret_rotate, secret_metadata_change, role_assignment, break_glass_issue}
- actor: principal (type:name) e.g., user:marina.lopez or svc:billing-worker
- target_path: vault path or credential id
- target_version: (optional) version number for rotated secrets
- action_result: success | failure | partial
- auth_method: token | app_role | oidc | hsm
- request_id: trace id to correlate across infra
- client_ip: x-forwarded-for if available
- session_id: optional session identifier for break-glass sessions
- reason: free text, required for break_glass events and role assignments
- evidence_refs: list of artifact ids produced by evidence-collector (filenames or urls)

Example SIEM export mapping (Splunk/Elastic friendly)
- index: redwood-secrets-audit
- doc._id -> event_id
- @timestamp -> timestamp
- source -> vault-audit-log
- fields: actor,target_path,event_type,action_result,session_id,request_id,client_ip,reason,evidence_refs
- Tag break-glass events with severity: high and set ecs.label: ["break_glass","investigate_immediately"]

Evidence automation pattern (how we collect and store)
- evidence-collector microservice responsibilities:
  - Subscribe to vault-audit events with filter: target_path ~ "/secret/" or event_type in rotate/delete/break_glass
  - For every relevant event, snapshot:
    - Last 12 hours of audit events for the target request_id
    - Current RBAC bindings for the target path (API: /rbac/v2/bindings?path=<>)
    - Active sessions list for principals involved
    - KMS/HSM access logs (if HSM key used)
  - Package snapshots into a timestamped artifact (tar.gz), store in evidence-bucket with retention metadata, and emit evidence_ref in SIEM and ticketing system.
- Retention default: 180 days (adjustable by compliance), with longer retention for PCI/HIPAA impacted tenants.

Credential inventory hygiene (notes and checklist)
- Inventory canonical fields: credential_id, path, owner, team, env, created_at, last_rotated, rotation_cadence, risk_level, downstream_consumers (list), deprecation_date, tags.
- Quarterly inventory audit: automate check that every credential has owner and rotation_cadence set. Flag exceptions to SecOps.
- Decommission flow: mark credential.deprecation_date, notify downstream consumers 14/7/3 days before auto-disable; after disable, hold in read-only for 7 days, then delete per policy.

Deconfliction & edge-cases (notes from earlier incidents)
- Race condition: simultaneous rotation by rotation-controller and manual patch -> ensure rotation-controller uses optimistic locking via metadata.version.
- Cross-team ownership ambiguity: if no owner listed, default to infra-team on-call until owner is assigned. Create ticket auto-assignment rule.
- HSM key rollovers: require offline coordination; include manual checkpoint steps and runbook dry-run at least 7 days before scheduled rollover.

Instrumentation & dashboards
- Minimum dashboards: rotation success rate, average time-to-rotate, number of break-glass events (last 30/90 days), pending role-change approvals, evidence collector failures.
- Alerts: rotation failure >3% / day, evidence-collector job error, SIEM missing required fields for break-glass events.

Open action items / TODOs
- [ ] Finalize RBAC role names and publish mapping to product teams (owner: Priya) — due 2026-02-28
- [ ] Implement evidence-collector connector to Elastic ingest pipeline (owner: Darren) — P0 for Q1 2026
- [ ] Add rotation-controller optimistic-lock logic and backoff (owner: Omar) — in PR review
- [ ] Add automated owner-assignment for orphaned credentials (owner: security-automation)

References and links
- Confluence: SEC-VAULT-ARCH-2025 (architecture notes and diagrams)
- GitHub: infra/vault-rotation-scripts (rotation-controller)
- Jira: SEC-1347 (RBAC v2 rollout epic)

Notes to self / freeform brainstorm (keep here while drafting)
- Consider adding 'rotation windows' per service SLAs (e.g., 02:00-05:00 pacific) to reduce blast radius at peak traffic times.
- Investigate audit event enrichment at proxy layer (add user-agent / deployment-id to events).
- Might want a 'rotation dry-run' flag that runs smoke tests without swapping references; useful for canaries.

Contact list for escalation: Marina Lopez (owner), Priya Nambiar (RBAC), Darren Cho (evidence-collector), On-call SecOps (rotation pager).

Last edited notes: moved SIEM mapping to ECS-friendly fields on 2026-02-18. This doc will be split into small runnable tickets during next sprint planning.
